responsibility: Main C++ expression type-checking implementation. It completes types on demand, builds and validates typed expressions and conversions, checks lvalue/rvalue and value-category rules, pointer arithmetic and comparison semantics, address/reference/member-pointer operations, return-expression validity, argument conversions, literal-operator constraints, and many core expression semantics used by the parser and semantic layer before lowering. It also owns important post-call-construction semantic checks for typed call expressions and their arguments, including cases that later interact with C-family attribute and format diagnostics. It differs from call.cc by handling general expression well-formedness after overload/call construction, and differs from constexpr.cc by checking ordinary semantic validity rather than executing expressions as constants.
same_name_distinction: Use this file for bugs where a C++ expression or call has already been parsed/selected but its typed semantic validity, conversions, value category, or argument checking are wrong. Use call.cc for overload candidate collection and overload ranking, pt.cc for template substitution machinery, error.cc for diagnostic formatting, and c-family/c-format.cc for the format-warning implementation itself.
